Er, the habit I want to change is my phone, I look my phone too much in the night.
Every night I go to the bed at eleven o'clock, but after I take my phone and I watch videos.
Sometimes I sleep at two o'clock in the morning.
I have this habit since two year, I think it start after the pandemic.
Before I read a book in the night but now I don't read.
In the morning I am very tired and I don't want to wake up.
In the class I cannot listen the teacher and I forget many thing.
Also my eyes is hurt in the afternoon.
It is difficult because the phone is always near my bed, and I say one video only but after it become five video.
I try to put the phone in the other room but after three days I forget.
Yes, this is my bad habit.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The talk continues and touches all four points, but each point is skimmed in one sentence and the same pattern (In the morning / In the class / Also) repeats in the effects section. The difficulty point is packed into a single long sentence.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary describing the habit is next to none: habit, phone, video, tired repeat. "One video only, but after it become five video" is a good attempt but does not land in the right form.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Tense and agreement errors are in most sentences (I look my phone, I have this habit since two year, it start, my eyes is hurt), and plural markers drop (two year, many thing, five video). Structures are simple; there is no complex structure beyond the two clauses built with because.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Tell the effects section through a single day — say what happened in which lesson — because at present three separate outcomes are listed in three separate sentences. Then fix the "since two year" structure: every sentence describing duration carries the same error.

answers.transcript:
The habit I would really like to change is looking at my phone before I sleep. It sounds like a small thing, but for me it's become a serious problem.
Every night I go to bed around eleven, and then I take my phone to check the notifications for two minutes.
And after that I start watching short videos, and when I look at the clock again it's one o'clock or half past one in the morning.
I have this habit since more or less two years, I think it started in the pandemic period when we were all closed at home. Before that I used to read a book in the evening and I slept much better.
The effect on my day is bad. In the morning I'm exhausted, I need two coffees before I can speak with anybody, and in my classes I lose the concentration after twenty minutes.
And why is it difficult? Because the phone is next to my bed and it's the last thing that I see. And honestly these applications are made for you cannot stop, this is their job.
I tried to leave the phone in the kitchen, but after three or four days I forgot, and everything came back like before.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points are developed and a section is opened with a question of its own, such as "And why is it difficult?", which carries the flow. On the other hand the effects section turns into a list, and links repeat with and / because / also.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is vocabulary to carry the topic (notifications, exhausted, headaches, pandemic period), and meaning is never closed off. It slips in two places: "I lose the concentration", "we were all closed at home".
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: used to, the past tense, a time clause and an indirect question are formed; most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors sit in a narrow set: the duration structure (I have this habit since two years), the construction "made for you cannot stop", "came back like before".

answers.what_would_lift_it: Properly form the sentence "These applications are made for you cannot stop" — the idea is the response's best idea, but the structure collapses. Also move to the present perfect for duration (I've had this habit for two years).

answers.transcript:
The habit I'd change, without a doubt, is scrolling on my phone in bed. It sounds trivial when you say it out loud, but it's got completely out of hand.
The pattern is always the same. I get into bed at about eleven, I pick up my phone just to check my messages, two minutes, that's the plan, and then one video leads into another and suddenly it's half one in the morning and I couldn't tell you a single thing I've watched.
I've been doing it for a good two years now. It crept up on me during the lockdowns, when there wasn't a lot else to do, and it never really went away. Before that I used to read for half an hour and I slept like a log.
The knock-on effect is what actually bothers me. I'm shattered in the mornings, I'm useless before my second coffee, and by the middle of a lecture I've lost the thread completely. It's not that the material is harder, I mean, it's not the material at all, I'm just running on four hours' sleep.
And as for why it's so hard to break, partly the phone is right there on the pillow, and partly these apps are designed by very clever people whose whole job is making sure you don't stop.
I did try leaving it in the kitchen overnight, and it worked brilliantly, for about four days.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The talk is comfortable and sections connect on their own ("The pattern is always the same", "The knock-on effect is what actually bothers me"). There is one self-correction ("it's not that the material is harder, I mean, it's not the material at all"), the rare kind of correction that eight lines allow.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items are plentiful and accurate: out of hand, crept up on me, slept like a log, knock-on effect, shattered, lost the thread, running on four hours' sleep, hard to break. Idioms settle in without strain.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Structural range is wide: the present perfect continuous (I've been doing it), relative clauses (whose whole job is), the "It's not that ..." structure, the passive. Errors are rare and do not stop the listener.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target. For the next level up, the idea of "design" in the final section needs to be taken a little further; at present it is left in one sentence and closed with a joke.
